architecture-core.decision: Where each Tier 1 fix lives: the shared hook/conformance path once for all hosts, with host adapters only rendering, so Claude, Codex and Copilot cannot diverge again (B4F-107, B4F-108, B4F-096).

requirements-nfr.decision: The Tier 1 acceptance evidence and stop: the B4F-108 cross-host workshop test, the per-scenario before/after friction protocol, and what counts as a real decision versus a corrective exchange.

ui-ux.decision: The human-facing contract for repeated and degraded states: one crossing presentation per session (B4F-104), proportionate recovery for a missing dials line (B4F-106), dials as prose on every host (B4F-107), refusals that name the step or cause (B4F-102, B4F-108), and the late orientation demand (B4F-096).

observability-resilience.decision: How a transient journal-lock failure recovers instead of latching, and how any degraded capture state is disclosed to the human and agent rather than silently consuming turns (B4F-108).

security-compliance.decision: How hook output is still kept from counting as human authority while capture is degraded, without blocking every typed reply (the trust rule behind the B4F-108 marker).

data-storage.decision: Which on-disk record is authoritative for the current feature and work (B4F-105, B4F-089), and the fixed ignored location for turn drafts (B4F-101).

code-implementation.decision: Confirm the inherited PowerShell craft rules and test posture for engine fixes, plus the reviewer host and authorization for this feature.

skipped.component-design: No new components; every fix changes behaviour inside existing hook, conformance, status and renderer scripts, and architecture-core already decides placement.
skipped.integration-api: No new or changed external API or host hook-event contract; host parity is verified by the B4F-108 cross-host test owned by requirements-nfr.
skipped.devops-operations: No pipeline or deployment change in scope; B4F-103 is a comparison correction with no beta4 republish, and beta4.1 publication is a later separate decision.

architecture-core.decision: Agreed with amendments: (1) content and decisions are made once in the shared path; adapters own host mechanics only, namely input normalization into a standard turn record {event, typed user text, host} under a declared tested contract, plus output emission of shared text as-is, and never choose wording or values or decide whether a reply counts; (2) keep the existing layered hook structure, no new components; (3) the cross-host test runs through each real adapter with recorded real Claude/Codex/Copilot hook payloads as fixtures, never a direct shared-path call; B4F-108 adds a fault-injection test (forced journal-lock collision: capture recovers, degraded state disclosed, hook output still cannot count as human).

requirements-nfr.decision: Agreed with amendments: quality priority is authority integrity, cross-host parity, diagnosability, friction, latency (diagnosability raised above friction because the real cost was a refusal naming the wrong cause). Friction protocol: real decisions vs corrective exchanges vs extra stops, before/after per scenario, elapsed split where observable, null not zero; B4F-108 baselines add Codex several corrective rounds never closed, Claude one round, and the 2026-09-09..2026-10-13 silent outage as not captured. Thresholds: each finding required behavior plus 0 corrective exchanges and 0 extra stops; B4F-108 adds 3 receipts at 1 reply per checkpoint per host and same-turn disclosure with 0 silently consumed turns under injected fault. Iteration-1 closeout verdict is the Tier 1 acceptance. No recorded hook payloads exist; capturing real Claude/Codex/Copilot payloads is a Tier 1 task in scratch directories only.

agenda: Source of UX truth and degraded-state refusals
ui-ux.decision: Governing UX principle (maintainer, verbatim in ui-ux.md, ranks above all decisions): the human provides intent, reasons, directs and decides; the system analyzes, recommends, implements, validates and diagnoses its own failures; a stop only when a human decision is needed AND context is lacking; a question gets an answer, not a stop; unchanged context needs no packet; nothing needed means no message; packet size follows the context gap; verdicts stay explicit typed replies. Decisions: (1) refusal standard plus orientation contract; in degraded states the system diagnoses, self-recovers and asks only for a decision, and says whether the turn was consumed; (2) B4F-104 by context not frequency: answer questions, at most a brief mention while context is unchanged, full packet only after a context gap; (3) the hook never blocks over formatting, checks substance only, system-filled text is marked as system output and journaled; (4) one shared dials sentence, only the correction command reference from the adapter; (5) the meaning-bearing line set is declared once in the shared path, including verdict options. Applied to all Tier 1 findings; beyond-Tier-1 exposure recorded as B5F-004.

observability-resilience.decision: Agreed with amendments: (1) prevent the collision rather than only retry it: the dispatcher opens the journal with FileShare.Read so concurrent appends are guaranteed to fail; the write path must permit concurrent writers (compatible share mode or per-write cross-process lock), with bounded retry as a backup; persistent failures are exceptional and enter degraded; (2) degraded state self-clears on the next successful append and records recovery; a human decision only if self-recovery fails; migration: a marker left by an older version is an ordinary degraded state that clears on the next append; (3) disclose in the affected turn (including whether it was consumed), in status/where while degraded, and in session-start orientation; (4) health journal of transitions, hashes only; question passed to security: buffer unjournaled hook output and write it on recovery; (5) fault-injection cases a-d plus (e) two real hook processes appending concurrently both succeed with no degradation.
observability-resilience.diagram: specs/202-beta4-1-ux-stabilization/workshop/observability-resilience.md - journal health lifecycle today vs agreed

security-compliance.decision: Agreed with corrections: (1) precise fail-closed via a per-process outage buffer of hook-output hashes; the integrity check reads the journal plus buffer files before the next prompt-submit decision (no unchecked window); on recovery the buffer is flushed to the journal and the files are removed; if the buffer write also fails, only that turn fails closed and is disclosed in the same turn with its consumed status; blanket fail-closed and fail-open rejected. (2) Origin is a second line of defense, not a construction guarantee: values typed-user, host-injected and unknown (some hosts, e.g. Copilot 1.0.79, replay hook text as plain user prompts); only typed-user can mint, and the journal/buffer match applies to every reply. (3) The integrity stores hold hashes only. (4) Every human-approved recovery action records its approving receipt.
security-compliance.diagram: specs/202-beta4-1-ux-stabilization/workshop/security-compliance.md - trust boundary: adapter origin, receipt writer, journal and outage buffer

data-storage.decision: Agreed with amendments: (1) start-context.json is the single current-feature pointer (option a), kept current by every writer that creates or advances a feature; guard: the pointer records the branch it was written for, and on a branch mismatch readers treat it as stale, reconcile from the branch and the in-flight controller, and disclose; a Shipped/closed feature is never shown active while one is in flight; the human is asked only when two in-flight features compete; a test proves every feature writer updates the pointer. (2) Resume where-we-are lines come from disk only (pending crossing, from_commit..HEAD, progress); the handover narrative is context shown with its age and flagged when stale or naming another feature. (3) Turn draft per session at .specrew/runtime/turn-end/<session>/turn-message.md, resolved by the draft-saving script so the agent never needs its session id; a host that cannot support this is raised at design-analysis, never as a run-time stop.
data-storage.diagram: specs/202-beta4-1-ux-stabilization/workshop/data-storage.md - current-work records table and agreed branch-guarded read path

code-implementation.decision: Agreed with amendments: (1) inherit the 199 manifest (46 selections, carried custom rules rescoped to feature-202); the remote-main sync rule is replaced for 202 by syncing with the beta4 line origin/201-first-run-experience until the main merge is decided separately. (2) Concurrency scoped exception: share mode permitting concurrent journal appends first; a per-write cross-process lock on the hook-output journal only if fault-injection case (e) proves the share mode insufficient; no generic lock framework; outage buffer on unique per-process files. (3) Keep the banned-noun rule; recovery wording never implies data loss when nothing is lost (reference: Specrew could not record your reply safely. May I clear the stuck error so it can record again? Nothing is deleted.). (4) 199 test posture plus real-adapter recorded-payload cross-host test, fault-injection cases a-e with (e) on three OSes, the pointer-writer test; expected journal failures become disclosed degraded state. (5) No new dependency. (6) Reviewer codex, authorized as workshop-202-beta4-1-ux-stabilization; its file-delivery quirk (empty stdout, findings in .review/findings.jsonl, possible partial label) is not a review failure.
